result.title: SimplexLoRA: Dynamic Rank Updating via Alternating Minimization with Simplex Projection
result.summary: The success of large language models in real-world applications relies on parameter-efficient fine-tuning methods such as Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA), which inserts compact, trainable adapters into selected layers. In this paper, we propose SimplexLoRA, a LoRA variant that adaptively adjusts adapter ranks during fine-tuning based on their learned importance. Unlike standard LoRA, which employs a fixed rank across all layers, SimplexLoRA optimizes per-adapter importance weights on the $n$-scaled simplex during a short warm-up and then freezes them, dynamically allocating capacity where it is most beneficial without increasing the overall parameter budget or inference cost. We evaluate SimplexLoRA across 12 language understanding, summarization, and reasoning tasks using DeBERTaV3, BART-large, Llama 3.1 8B, and Qwen3-8B. Our results show that SimplexLoRA consistently matches or outperforms standard LoRA and recent adaptive baselines, with the largest gains at low ranks. Our code is available at https://github.com/brain-lab-research/SimplexLoRA.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 SimplexLoRA：在微调初期用交替最小化在 n 维单纯形上学习各适配器的重要性权重，随后冻结，按重要性动态分配 LoRA 秩，在不增加参数预算与推理成本下替代固定秩 LoRA，并在 12 个语言理解、摘要与推理任务上验证。
AI.relevance_reason: 该工作属纯文本 PEFT，与 VLM 推理无直接关联；但其「按学习到的重要性权重决定各模块容量分配」的机制可供核查是否能迁移到 latent 推理中为不同层或分支分配状态容量与监督权重。
